\[
f = 1 - a\, t^2 (3 - 2t),
\quad
t = \operatorname{clamp}\left(\frac{d - d_0}{1 - d_0}, 0, 1\right),
\qquad a = 50\,\%,\ d_0 = 50\,\%
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(d\): The distance from the center, 1 at the corners
- \(d_0\): The start
- \(a\): The amount
- \(f\): The factor on each pixel

d is the distance from the center of the image, measured on an ellipse with the shape of the image, so that the corners are at 1. Below the start d_0 nothing changes. Beyond it, the factor falls smoothly along the smoothstep curve t^2 (3 - 2t), down to 1 - a at the corners. This falloff is PixelNexus's own. Real lenses lose light toward the corners for several reasons, and their curves differ. With Linear light on, f multiplies the linear light values, as a loss of light does.
